cf.title: PoC: Simplify recovery after dropping a table by LOGGING the restore LSN
cf.authors: Nikolay Shaplov (nataraj), Andrey Borodin (x4m), Kirk Wolak (kirkw), Dmitry Lebedev (dmitrylebedev), Salma El-Sayed (salmae)

input.subject: PoC: Simplify recovery after dropping a table by LOGGING the restore LSN

verdict_reasoning: The goal has support from reviewers, but the case for core code is not yet made. [P7] proposed the same setting for DROP TABLE and TRUNCATE and was rejected because event triggers can do it. already-exists-1 shows that an sql_drop event trigger logging the xid gives an exact target through recovery_target_xid. maintenance-fit-1 shows that the thread does not answer the extension question for v13.

brief.title: Log the recovery LSN when a permanent table is dropped or truncated
brief.problem: A user who drops or truncates the wrong table must find the LSN just before the drop to do point-in-time recovery. The authors call this a common support request. Finding that LSN by hand is slow and error-prone.
brief.proposed_design: With a new GUC enabled, the server writes a LOG line with the commit LSN for each committed permanent table drop or truncate, with a hint to use recovery_target_lsn and recovery_target_inclusive = false. Since v13 the line is written in RecordTransactionCommit right after the commit record. Rolled-back work, temporary and unlogged tables, prepared transactions and wal_level = minimal produce no line.
user_visible_surface: GUC log_object_drops (default off); the reviewer says the name may change.
Server LOG message per table, e.g. table "public.t" (OID 16384) dropped at LSN X/X, with a recovery hint.
Documentation of the GUC, including the prepared transaction and wal_level = minimal exclusions.
author_claims: Accidental table drops are an all too common support request.
Recovering to the logged LSN with recovery_target_inclusive = false brings the table back.
An extension cannot easily do this, because the object access hook runs before commit, when the commit LSN does not exist yet.
The message is logged even when a backend is killed while waiting for synchronous replication after commit.
brief.thread_state: Jim Jones, Zsolt Parragi, Kirill Reshke and Andrey Borodin reviewed; DROP DATABASE was removed from scope by agreement, and v13 is the latest. Open points are the GUC name, the missing database name in the default log prefix, and a possible TAP test for the SyncRep case.
unclear: The material does not say whether a commit-path log line adds measurable cost when the GUC is on and many tables are dropped, for example by DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE.
The material does not say who may set log_object_drops (superuser, per session, or only in postgresql.conf).
The material does not say how users find the log line on a standby or with a log_line_prefix that lacks the database.
The thread does not answer Kirill Reshke's question about doing this in an extension once the patch uses xact.c hooks directly.

prior_attempts.title: automatic restore point
prior_attempts.quote: Right now, you just have it hardcoded to TRUNCATE and DROP TABLE, which seems somewhat arbitrary. With event triggers, you have the full flexibility to do what you want.
prior_attempts.reason: Reviewers said the same result is possible without core changes, through event triggers or the utility hook, and that a hardcoded set of commands is arbitrary and hard to extend. Michael Paquier also called the conditions hard to define and the gain small next to backups and delayed standbys. He rejected the patch because it brings nothing that event triggers cannot do.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: This proposal logs the exact commit LSN from RecordTransactionCommit and skips rolled-back, temporary, unlogged and two-phase cases. P7 logged an LSN, or created a restore point, before the command ran.

objections.title: Event triggers with recovery_target_xid already give an exact recovery target
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA creates an sql_drop event trigger that does `raise log` with pg_current_xact_id() and the dropped object names. After an accidental DROP TABLE, the DBA sets recovery_target_xid to the logged xid with recovery_target_inclusive = false, and recovery stops just before that commit. Core would then carry a second, narrower mechanism and a new GUC for the same job.
objections.argument: Message #6 says an extension cannot log the commit LSN before commit. That holds for an LSN, but recovery_target_xid needs no commit LSN, and the xid is known when the drop runs. [P7] was rejected for this reason: event triggers already do it, and a fixed list of commands is arbitrary. Event triggers do not fire on TRUNCATE, so the real gap is TRUNCATE and convenience, and the thread argues neither.
objections.author_must_show: What does the commit-LSN log line give that an sql_drop event trigger logging the xid for recovery_target_xid cannot, apart from TRUNCATE coverage?

critic.reasoning: recovery_target_xid with recovery_target_inclusive = false stops just before that commit, and the xid is known when sql_drop fires. The thread's answer in message #6 covers only LSN targets, so the remaining gap is TRUNCATE and convenience, as the objection says.

objections.title: Earlier rejection on extension grounds not yet answered for v13
objections.failure_scenario: A committer reads [P7], which was rejected because event triggers could do the same, and asks why core must own this. The thread gives no answer for the current design. The patch stalls on the same question that ended [P7].
objections.argument: Message #3 asks why an extension cannot do this, and message #6 answers that an extension would need an xact callback plus savepoint tracking. Extensions can already do both. Moving the logging into RecordTransactionCommit (message #21) creates a real gap for the SyncRep kill case, but the thread never states that gap as the reason core is needed. [P7] recorded the same objection for the same pair of commands.
objections.author_must_show: Why is the SyncRep kill window from message #20 serious enough to need core code, and could a small generic post-commit hook close it for an extension instead?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 lists what an extension would need, and extensions already have object access hooks, xact callbacks and the commit LSN. The thread never states the SyncRep kill case as the reason for core code, and Kirill Reshke's question has no answer for v13.

other_surviving.title: Log line does not identify the database of the dropped table
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A DBA runs several databases cloned with create database ... template. A user in one of them drops public.t, and the log shows several lines like table "public.t" (OID 16384) dropped at LSN X/X. With the default log_line_prefix, the DBA cannot tell which line belongs to the damaged database and may pick the wrong LSN for PITR.
other_surviving.argument: Message #22 says that the default text-log prefix has no database name, and that cloned databases share table names and OIDs. v13 has no answer to this yet. The OID does not tell the databases apart in this case, so the message is the only reliable place to say which database the table was in. The point of the feature is a correct recovery target, so a line that can be ambiguous weakens the user-facing contract.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Will the message include the database name, or how does a user with the default log_line_prefix match a line to the right database?

critic.reasoning: Message #22 raises this and v13 has no answer yet. A user can add %d to log_line_prefix, but the default prefix lacks it and cloned databases share names and OIDs, so the line can be ambiguous.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: GUC name and scope fix an arbitrary command set into the contract
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A DBA enables log_object_drops, expecting to be protected from accidental data loss. A user then runs drop materialized view, alter table ... drop column, or delete without a where clause, and nothing is logged. The DBA learns about the gap when no LSN exists at recovery time.
other_surviving.argument: Message #19 notes that the name says "object drops", while v13 covers only permanent tables and also covers TRUNCATE. Message #21 defers the rename. A boolean named after objects invites later releases to add more commands, and then the same setting logs more after an upgrade without the user asking for it. [P7] rejected a setting for the same pair of commands partly because a hardcoded TRUNCATE and DROP TABLE set looked arbitrary.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What name and value type (boolean, or a list of commands) will the setting have, so that later additions do not silently change what existing configurations log?

critic.reasoning: Message #19 confirms the name does not match the scope, and message #21 defers the rename without stating a scope rule. [P7] should be used only for the scope point, because its recorded reason was mainly that event triggers suffice.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Log call placed between commit record and ProcArray end can turn errors into PANIC
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user runs drop schema ... cascade on a schema with many thousands of tables, with log_object_drops on. The commit record is already flushed when the patch builds one LOG message per table. If any allocation or log write raises an ERROR there, the abort path finds an already-committed transaction and the server PANICs.
other_surviving.argument: Message #21 moves the logging into RecordTransactionCommit right after END_CRIT_SECTION, so it now runs after the commit record and before ProcArrayEndTransaction. In that window an ERROR cannot be turned into an abort, and RecordTransactionAbort raises PANIC for a transaction whose commit record exists. The proposal does not say why work that grows with the number of dropped tables cannot fail at this point. It also does not say why the logging could not run after the transaction is visible as committed.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What guarantees that the per-table logging between the commit record and ProcArrayEndTransaction cannot raise an ERROR, even when one transaction drops thousands of tables?

critic.reasoning: An ERROR after the commit record does lead to PANIC in the abort path, and the thread does not say why the new code cannot raise one. The risk is narrower than stated, since interrupts are held there and SyncRepWaitForLSN already emits WARNINGs in that window.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Proposal does not say who may set log_object_drops
other_surviving.failure_scenario: An administrator sets log_object_drops = on in postgresql.conf and relies on it for recovery. If the GUC is user-settable, a role that owns tables can run set log_object_drops to off before a drop or truncate. The administrator learns there is no LSN only when recovery is needed.
other_surviving.argument: Messages #9 and #17 enable the GUC with a session-level SET, and the material never names its context. Comparable settings that control what reaches the server log, such as log_statement and log_min_messages, are superuser-only so that ordinary sessions cannot remove entries the administrator asked for. The drop LSN is only useful if every drop is logged once the administrator turns the setting on. A committer would likely ask that the context follow that existing practice, or that the proposal explain why it does not.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Is log_object_drops PGC_SUSET or stricter, and if not, why should an ordinary session be able to turn off this logging?

critic.reasoning: The material does not name the GUC context, and the brief lists this as unclear. log_statement and log_min_messages are superuser-only, so a committer would likely ask for the same here or for a stated reason to differ.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Earlier rejection reason, that event triggers suffice, is only partly answered
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA who wants this today writes an event trigger on sql_drop that logs pg_current_wal_insert_lsn(). After an accidental drop, they restore to a side instance at that LSN and copy the table back. Core then carries a GUC and a hook in RecordTransactionCommit for a gain that is small in that workflow.
refuted.argument: [P7] proposed nearly the same feature (a log_recovery_points setting for DROP TABLE and TRUNCATE) and was rejected because event triggers can do it. Message #6 answers that only the commit LSN is exact, and message #3 notes the insert LSN can be earlier under load. An earlier LSN still restores the table, though. It only loses concurrent commits, which matters less when the table is copied back from a side instance. Kirill Reshke's extension question (message #3) was not revisited after v13 moved the logging into xact.c (message #21).
refuted.author_must_show: In which recovery workflows does the exact commit LSN save data that an event trigger logging the pre-drop insert LSN would lose?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1, which makes the same event-trigger point with an exact target (the xid) and also names the TRUNCATE gap. This version rests on an inexact insert LSN and does not note that event triggers do not fire on TRUNCATE.

refuted.title: The covered command set keeps the shape P7 called arbitrary
refuted.failure_scenario: A user turns on the GUC, expecting a recovery LSN for destructive DDL, and then runs alter table ... drop column, or drop materialized view. No line is written. They find out only when they search the log after the data is gone.
refuted.argument: The recorded key sentence of [P7] objects to a set hardcoded to TRUNCATE and DROP TABLE, and v13 covers that same pair. Message #1 listed DROP DATABASE, DELETE and UPDATE as candidates. DROP DATABASE was removed in message #13, and message #19 notes that the GUC name no longer matches the scope. The proposal does not say which rule decides what is covered, so it gives later patches no guide for adding commands.
refuted.author_must_show: What rule defines which commands log a recovery LSN, and how would a future destructive command be added under it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which covers the same scope question and adds the concrete point about the setting's name and value type.

refuted.title: Privilege level of log_object_drops is not stated
refuted.failure_scenario: If the setting is user-settable, an application role runs set log_object_drops = off, or a role-level setting does the same, and the role's drops leave no recovery line. The DBA finds out only at recovery time. A user-settable setting would also let any role fill the server log by creating and dropping many tables.
refuted.argument: Server-log settings such as log_statement and log_min_duration_statement are superuser-only, because they control what the DBA sees. The thread and the documentation hunks do not say which context v13 uses. The feature only helps when the DBA can rely on every drop being logged, so the context belongs in the user-facing contract.
refuted.author_must_show: Which GUC context does log_object_drops use, and why does it match the existing log_* settings?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of security-1, which cites the session-level SET examples in the thread. The log-flooding addition applies only when the setting is on, and a role that can create and drop tables can already fill the log through other log_* settings.

refuted.title: Logged LSN can point to WAL that is lost after failover
refuted.failure_scenario: The primary logs "dropped at LSN X" before the standby confirms the commit, then fails, and the standby is promoted without that commit. Later a DBA restores a base backup with recovery_target_lsn = X and the default latest timeline. Recovery then stops at X on the new timeline, which is unrelated WAL, and nothing tells the DBA that the restored state is wrong.
refuted.argument: Messages #20 and #21 log the LSN on purpose before the SyncRep wait, so the line can describe a commit that never became durable on the surviving node. The hint in the log line names only recovery_target_lsn and recovery_target_inclusive. It does not name the timeline the LSN belongs to, and the documentation hunks in the material do not cover failover or timeline switches.
refuted.author_must_show: How does a user who restores after a failover know which timeline the logged LSN belongs to, and should the log line or hint include the timeline ID?

critic.reasoning: In the scenario the promoted standby never replayed the drop, so the table still exists there and no recovery to that LSN is needed. LSNs without a timeline are existing practice for recovery_target_lsn and for other server log lines such as checkpoint messages.

refuted.title: Fixed command list invites a new special case per release
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs alter table ... drop column, or a delete without a where clause, on the wrong table, with log_object_drops = on. Nothing is logged, and the user finds out while searching the log during recovery. The next patch then adds that command to the same commit-path code.
refuted.argument: Message #1 already lists DROP DATABASE, DELETE and UPDATE as candidates, and DROP DATABASE was deferred to a later patch (messages #13-#15). [P7] called a hardcoded TRUNCATE and DROP TABLE list arbitrary. Each future destructive command must register itself, and nothing fails when a new data-removing path does not. Jim notes in message #19 that the GUC name already fits the scope poorly.
refuted.author_must_show: Which rule decides what a future command must log, and how would a reviewer notice a new destructive path that does not register?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. The claim that later patches will add commands to the commit path is a guess; the thread removed DROP DATABASE from scope and message #3 advised against DELETE and UPDATE.

refuted.title: Per-table logging inside RecordTransactionCommit before the SyncRep wait
refuted.failure_scenario: With the GUC on, a drop schema ... cascade of thousands of partitions writes thousands of LOG lines in the commit path while it still holds its locks. If the log pipe is slow, other sessions wait longer on those locks. An error raised in that window, after the commit record, would turn into a PANIC.
refuted.argument: Since message #21, the logging runs after END_CRIT_SECTION and before the transaction is fully committed. That window in RecordTransactionCommit has been kept small on purpose. The thread shows no measurement for a many-table drop, and it does not say why no error can be raised there. Every later change to RecordTransactionCommit must keep this new code safe.
refuted.author_must_show: What is the commit latency for a cascaded drop of many tables with the GUC on, and what guarantees nothing in the new logging can raise an error?

critic.reasoning: The PANIC part is a duplicate of replication-ondisk-1. The latency cost falls only on installations that turn the setting on, and the locks held longer are on tables that the same transaction is dropping.

refuted.title: Demand rests on the authors' support experience, and a 2018 version was rejected
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer reads "all too common support request" in message #1 and finds no counts, reports or user requests. The same idea was rejected in 2018 as doable with event triggers. Without new evidence, the patch is likely to stall at the same point.
refuted.argument: The only demand statement in the material is the authors' claim in message #1. Message #3 adds that the change is useful but doubts it belongs in core. [P7] proposed nearly the same setting for DROP TABLE and TRUNCATE and was rejected because event triggers can log an LSN before the drop. Message #6 answers that only the commit LSN is exact, but it does not show how often the earlier LSN from an event trigger, or a pg_waldump search for the commit record, fails real users.
refuted.author_must_show: How many recovery cases per year does your support see, and how often did an event-trigger LSN or a pg_waldump search fail to bring the table back?

critic.reasoning: The material shows demand that lasted: an independent author proposed the same feature in 2018 ([P7]), and reviewers in messages #2 and #3 call it useful. The event-trigger part is a duplicate of already-exists-1.

refuted.title: Default-off GUC misses most users who drop the wrong table
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on a default install drops the wrong table and asks for help. log_object_drops was off, so the log has no LSN, and support goes back to searching WAL by hand. The feature helps only sites that planned for the accident.
refuted.argument: The brief and message #4 say log_object_drops defaults to off. The users the problem statement describes are people who made a mistake, and those people are often not the ones who tuned logging settings ahead of time. Sites careful enough to enable it can already install an event trigger. The thread does not discuss who would turn the setting on, or whether it could default to on.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users would enable log_object_drops in advance but not already run an event trigger, and could the setting safely default to on?

critic.reasoning: This applies to every default-off logging setting, and PITR itself needs WAL archiving set up in advance. Setting one GUC cluster-wide is a lower bar than an event trigger in each database, and event triggers do not cover TRUNCATE.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The logging runs in RecordTransactionCommit after the commit record and before the SyncRep wait, and the line gives a recovery target.

touch_points.label: new GUC
touch_points.reason: The patch adds log_object_drops, and reviewers already question whether the name fits the scope.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The proposal does not state the GUC context, so an ordinary session may be able to turn the logging off.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: New code in the commit path must stay error-free, and the covered command set may grow.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: With the GUC on, the commit path writes one LOG line per dropped or truncated table.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: [P7] was rejected because event triggers can do the same, and message #3 asks the extension question again.

questions: What does the commit-LSN log line give that an sql_drop event trigger logging the xid for recovery_target_xid cannot, apart from TRUNCATE coverage?
Is the SyncRep kill case from message #20 the reason core code is needed, and could a generic post-commit hook let an extension cover it?
What guarantees that the per-table logging after the commit record cannot raise an ERROR when one transaction drops thousands of tables?
What name and value type will the setting have, and what rule decides which commands it covers?
Which GUC context does log_object_drops use, and will the message include the database name?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the commit path in xact.c and synchronous replication would have to own it. The visible thread and the CommitFest entry show reviewers but no such committer.
committability.liability: The owner signs for new code between the commit record and the end of the transaction, where an ERROR becomes a PANIC, for as long as the GUC exists. The owner also signs for the GUC name and scope.
committability.author_follow_up: The patch reached v13 over two years, and an author moved the entry to a new CommitFest in October 2026, so the authors appear to stay with it.

priority.reason: Sites that run PITR would benefit, and reviewers call the feature useful. The core-versus-event-trigger question from [P7] and the GUC name, scope and context need answers before code review; no patch code was read.

provisional_note: Without the code, the review could not check whether the logging in RecordTransactionCommit can raise an ERROR, or which GUC context v13 uses. Four level 2 objections survived (standards-compat-1, standards-compat-2, replication-ondisk-1, security-1) but are not ranked because level 1b fails first.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve recovery performance of dropping database having many tablespaces
precedents_retrieved.summary: DROP DATABASE would write one XLOG_DBASE_DROP record listing all tablespaces of the database, instead of one record per tablespace. On a standby, replay would then scan shared_buffers once, not once per tablespace.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers supported the idea and found the patch logically correct, but asked for performance numbers that show the recovery gain. One tester saw no difference with the patch, and Simon Riggs asked to rename tablespace_num to ntablespaces. The author did not respond for about two and a half months while the patch waited on author, so Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This was a couple of months ago, and nothing has happened since with the
patch waiting on author, so the patch is marked as returned with
feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent ALTER TABLE DROP NOT NULL on child tables if parent column has it
precedents_retrieved.summary: Prevent ALTER TABLE ... DROP NOT NULL on a child table when the same column in a parent table is marked NOT NULL, so that the constraint can only be dropped from the parent. The patch added a function in pg_inherits.c to list a relation's parents and a new index on pg_inherits.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the approach was wrong because it does not help decide whether to propagate DROP NOT NULL from a parent to its children, and pointed to the earlier plan of storing NOT NULL constraints in pg_constraint with inheritance counts as CHECK constraints do. After Vitaly Burovoy reported that he was writing such a patch, which already forbids dropping inherited NOT NULLs, the author withdrew his proposal in favour of that work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This doesn't sound like the right approach; in particular, it won't really
help for deciding whether to propagate a DROP NOT NULL on a parent rel to
its children.

precedents_retrieved.title: drop/truncate table sucks for large values of shared buffers
precedents_retrieved.summary: Speed up DROP/TRUNCATE TABLE when shared_buffers is large by looking up each block of the relation in the buffer mapping table, instead of scanning all of shared_buffers. This path is used only when the table is smaller than a threshold (25% of shared_buffers) and shared_buffers is at least 32MB.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the approach fails badly if the caller is wrong about the relation's maximum page number (for example, kernel lseek bugs). He also noted that it does not help DROP TABLESPACE or DROP DATABASE, which also scan the whole buffer pool. Heikki Linnakangas returned it with feedback, citing the issues raised, a still-unwritten alternative (delayed cleanup during the checkpoint scan), and a preference for a structure such as a radix tree that can find all buffers for a relation or database. Tom Lane added that committing a band-aid would make more complete fixes harder to pursue.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Committing a band-aid will just make it harder to pursue real fixes.

precedents_retrieved.title: Close race in DROP TABLESPACE on Windows
precedents_retrieved.summary: On Windows, DROP TABLESPACE can fail with "tablespace is not empty" because another backend still holds an open descriptor on an unlinked file, which Windows keeps in the directory. Noah Misch proposed that DROP TABLESPACE wait for other backends to close such files, for example by polling with a new wait_unlinked_files() function.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No code was written. Noah Misch recorded the fix as a TODO and changed the regression test to use RESET ROLE instead of \c -, so only one backend is involved. Amit Kapila said the wait could last until the other backend runs another command. Alternatives (a catchup interrupt, renaming files to the tablespace top-level directory before unlink) were left for whoever decides to work on the issue.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think we can discuss further about which approach is better, once someone decides to work on this issue.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add callback table access method to reset filenode when dropping relation
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a relation_reset_filenode callback to the table access method interface, called from heap_drop_with_catalog when a table is dropped, as the counterpart of relation_set_new_filenode. The goal was to let table AMs with non-file storage, such as an in-memory table, clean up their storage on DROP TABLE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund and Heikki Linnakangas pointed out that dropping storage must happen at commit or abort and be redone from the commit record during WAL replay, which cannot run AM-specific code. A callback at drop time, or xact callbacks run at commit, therefore cannot drop storage correctly. Heikki suggested using smgrGetPendingDeletes() instead. The patch then stopped applying, the author did not reply when asked whether he was waiting for feedback, and the entry was marked Returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't think implementing dropping relation data at-commit/rollback using
xact callbacks can be correct. The dropping needs to be integrated with the
commit / abort records, so it is redone during crash recovery - that's not
possible with xact callbacks.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prepare Transaction support for ON COMMIT DROP temporary tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows PREPARE TRANSACTION when every temporary table the transaction accessed was created with ON COMMIT DROP. PreCommit_on_commit_actions() drops those tables before the prepare, so the existing check against temporary tables in prepared transactions is relaxed for this case.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier showed that after creating an ON COMMIT DROP temp table and preparing, a client can disconnect but the backend stays waiting for a lock on its temporary schema until COMMIT PREPARED. The patch also does not handle the case where the temp table creates the session's temporary schema, and Tom Lane noted that tables without an ON COMMIT clause are not tracked. The entry was returned with feedback because more work was needed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This causes the client to think that the session is finished, but if
you look closer at the backend it is still pending to close until the
transaction is COMMIT PREPARED:

precedents_retrieved.title: automatic restore point
precedents_retrieved.summary: Create a restore point automatically, or log the current LSN to the server log, before destructive commands so a DBA can run PITR to just before an accidental data loss. The first design used pg_create_restore_point() for TRUNCATE, DROP, DELETE/UPDATE without WHERE and COPY FROM; the later patch added a log_recovery_points setting that logs the LSN for DROP TABLE and TRUNCATE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said the same result is possible without core changes, through event triggers or the utility hook, and that a hardcoded set of commands is arbitrary and hard to extend. Michael Paquier also called the conditions hard to define and the gain small next to backups and delayed standbys. He rejected the patch because it brings nothing that event triggers cannot do.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Right now, you just
have it hardcoded to TRUNCATE and DROP TABLE, which seems somewhat
arbitrary.  With event triggers, you have the full flexibility to do
what you want.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add last commit LSN to pg_last_committed_xact()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the LSN of the most recent commit to pg_last_committed_xact(), so monitoring can compute how far a logical slot lags behind the last commit. The first version stored the LSN in the commit_ts cache. A later version stored it in PGPROC on its own cache line, with a separate patch that makes pg_attribute_aligned work on MSVC.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry sat in waiting on author for longer than the commitfest threshold, so it was returned with feedback. The last visible review, by Michael Paquier in April, worried about making PGPROC larger and asked for changes to the configure and c.h handling in the MSVC patch. No author reply follows that review in the visible messages. Robert Haas had earlier questioned the cost of extra shared memory updates at commit.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This entry has been waiting on author input for a while (our current threshold is roughly two weeks), so I've marked it Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Restore lock level to update statusFlags
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Restore lock level to update statusFlags
Reverted commit(s): Relax lock level for setting PGPROC->statusFlags
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Reverts 27838981be9d (some comments are kept).  Per discussion, it does
not seem safe to relax the lock level used for this; in order for it to
be safe, there would have to be memory barriers between the point we set
the flag and the point we set the trasaction Xid, which perhaps would
not be so bad; but there would also have to be barriers at the readers'
side, which from a performance perspective might be bad.

Now maybe this analysis is wrong and it *is* safe for some reason, but
proof of that is not trivial.

precedents_retrieved.title: In INSERT/UPDATE, use the table's real tuple descriptor as target.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
In INSERT/UPDATE, use the table's real tuple descriptor as target.
Reverted commit(s): Fix corner case for a BEFORE ROW UPDATE trigger returning OLD.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Previously, ExecInitModifyTable relied on ExecInitJunkFilter,
and thence ExecCleanTypeFromTL, to build the target descriptor from
the query tlist.  While we just checked (in ExecCheckPlanOutput)
that the tlist produces compatible output, this is not a great
substitute for the relation's actual tuple descriptor that's
available from the relcache.  For one thing, dropped columns will
not be correctly marked attisdropped; it's a bit surprising that
we've gotten away with that this long.  But the real reason for
being concerned with this is that using the table's descriptor means
that the slot will have correct attrmissing data, allowing us to
revert the klugy fix of commit ba9f18abd.  (This commit undoes
that one's changes in trigger.c, but keeps the new test case.)
Thus we can solve the bogus-trigger-tuple problem with fewer cycles
rather than more.

No back-patch, since this doesn't fix any additional bug, and it
seems somewhat more likely to have unforeseen side effects than
ba9f18abd's narrow fix.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit a740b213d4b4d3360ad0cac696e47e5ec0eb8864.

Subsequent discussion showed that there was interest in a more general
facility to configure when server log events would produce backtraces,
and this existing limited way couldn't be extended in a compatible
way.  So the consensus was to revert this for PostgreSQL 17 and
reconsider this topic for PostgreSQL 18.

roaster_notes.note: P5 shares only the drop-at-commit area. Its reason concerns removing storage through xact callbacks and does not apply to a log line.
Three objections are listed. None is fatal from the standards and compatibility angle.

The proposal adds no WAL record, catalog, on-disk format or protocol change, so pg_upgrade and the wire protocol are not affected. The two objections concern only the commit path and how the logged LSN behaves under replication.
The log line reports only drops the session itself committed, and it is filtered to permanent tables, so it leaks no other users' data. The only security point found is the unstated GUC context.
Objections were raised. The thread has active reviewers, but the visible material does not name a committer who would own the commit-path change.
One objection. pg_waldump can also find the commit record of the drop by hand, but the brief already treats that way as slow.
Two objections raised. Reviewers in messages #2, #3 and #15 call the feature useful, but no independent user demand or field numbers appear in the material.
